_meta.name: XSSentinel Accuracy Benchmark
_meta.description: Independent positive/negative corpus for measuring detection accuracy (recall, precision, FPR). Each case defines a server reflection environment; the scanner generates its own payloads.

fields.param: query parameter name (empty string for DOM-only cases)
fields.mode: server reflection behavior (maps to server.py handler)
fields.ground_truth: vulnerable = should detect, safe = should NOT detect

location.hash -> innerHTML. Phase 161: declares dom_dynamic so this case can only be credited by the REAL BROWSER. Measured before: removing every DOM-family finding still left it TP via a trusted_types_taint_flow note, so a dead browser engine was invisible to the benchmark.

location.search -> eval. Phase 161: (a) param was empty, so the URL carried no query at all and the engine had no real parameter to swap -- the page reads a specific name, so the generic __xss__ probe could not reach it; the vector was unreachable and the case passed on static hints alone. Declaring the parameter the page actually consumes makes the flow testable. (b) The engine only hooked the Function constructor, never a direct eval(), so even with the right parameter it could not be confirmed -- fixed in dom_engine.py (Phase 161).

postMessage event.data -> innerHTML. Phase 161: declares dom_dynamic -- before, this case was also credited by a websocket_xss and a trusted_types note, so the browser engine was not what earned the verdict.
location.hash -> document.write. Phase 161: declares dom_dynamic (the browser is the only layer that proves it; a Trusted Types note used to credit it as well).

location.hash -> jQuery .html(). Phase 161: the page loads jQuery from code.jquery.com, so with no egress the library never arrives and the browser cannot run .html() -- requiring dom_dynamic here would make the case depend on the network. It therefore requires DOM-FAMILY evidence (dynamic confirmation OR the L3 static DOM hint) instead of the SRI/Trusted-Types collateral that used to credit it.

location.hash -> setTimeout string. Phase 161: declares dom_dynamic. Worth noting how this one hid a dead browser: with the engine ON the static L3 hint is SUPPRESSED by the dynamic confirmation, so the credited type is dom_dynamic; with the engine OFF the static `dom` hint surfaces and still credits the case -- the fallback masks the failure.

Phase 146: hash-ROUTED parameter (path is '#/route', so the probe URL is /#/route?q=) reaching innerHTML. The value lives inside the fragment's own query string behind a route path, so it is reachable only by parsing the fragment -- unlike pos-dom-01, which reads the whole fragment and is satisfied by the plain location.hash probe. This is the shape that hid both official XSS challenges on OWASP Juice Shop.

Phase 146: the safe twin of pos-dom-07 -- the identical router-shaped fragment written with textContent. Also the first DOM safe case in the manifest: the DOM layer previously had only vulnerable cases, so it was never checked for false positives.

Phase 151: the Trusted Types wrapper shape -- the fragment parameter reaches innerHTML as a NON-PRIMITIVE (real TrustedHTML via a permissive createPolicy when the runtime offers one, else a toString wrapper). The browser coerces via ToString and the payload executes, but the sink hook receives an object: the pre-Phase-144 has() (typeof v === 'string') went silent on EVERY assignment of such pages -- the whole innerHTML sink went dark on Angular/Juice Shop. Locks the String(v) contract in has().
Phase 151: the safe twin of pos-dom-08 -- the identical Trusted Types wrapper shape written with textContent (not a sink, no execution).

Phase 152: SPA-shaped stored XSS -- POST (form or JSON body) stores the comment verbatim; the view page never contains it in its HTML, it fetches /r/st02/list client-side and inserts the entries with innerHTML. Exactly the OWASP Juice Shop shape (POST /api/Feedbacks -> client-rendered admin route) where HTTP-text persistence verification is structurally blind; only the real-browser DOM engine can confirm.
Phase 152 safe twin: the value is HTML-escaped on write AND the SPA viewer inserts entries with textContent -- nothing executable is stored, nothing reaches an executable sink.

Phase 140 regression guard: an ordinary page loading a real CDN webfont (Google Fonts emits @font-face + unicode-range + external src:url()). Nothing is attacker-controlled, so it must NOT be reported -- this exact shape produced a high false positive on OWASP Juice Shop while both real XSS went unreported.

Phase 123: raw HTML reflection next to JS that consumes getElementById('cfg') and feeds it to innerHTML -- attacker-created id attributes win the lookup
Phase 123 safe twin: same page, same JS ref and sink, but a strip-tags sanitizer removes the ability to create an id/name attribute (escaping alone would NOT -- id=token stays textually visible)

Phase 123 FP lock: reflection is HTML-escaped, so no id/name attribute can be created -- but the text still reads id=<token>. The layer used to report dom_clobber here (high) purely from that textual match; fixed in dom_clobber.detect_reflection

Phase 124: real out-of-band confirmation. The app reflects raw markup and, link-unfurl style, resolves the src/href of REAL parsed elements -- so the injected <script src=callback> actually loads and the self-hosted listener receives the token. Confirms the whole inject -> beacon -> attribute chain without a browser.

Phase 124 safe twin: the same unfurler, but the value is HTML-escaped first, so no element is parsed and nothing can be resolved -> no beacon. The unfurler must be parser-aware (not a regex sweep for URLs), otherwise this twin would beacon off the escaped text and prove nothing.

Phase 125: the CSP fallback channel. Raw reflection under `script-src 'none'` -- the verifier refuses to confirm inline execution, so the standard loop fails and scan_time_based runs, injecting / / onerror-fetch resource payloads. The Phase 124 unfurler then really fetches them, so the tb_ token beacons and the layer confirms. Note the CSP must NOT be default-src none (that would block the very resources the layer depends on).
Phase 125 safe twin: same CSP, same unfurler, escaped reflection. No element or stylesheet is parsed, so the resource payload never loads and no token beacons -> the fallback correctly stays silent.

Phase 126: inject at A (POST, stores verbatim), verify at a DIFFERENT page B that renders what A stored -- raw. What makes this second-order is the A->B flow (CLI --second-order-inject/-viewers), not the handler.
Phase 126 safe twin: same two-page flow, but A stores the HTML-escaped value, so B renders it as text -- no executable context on the viewer, no second-order finding.

Phase 127: declarative multi-step scenario (L9_scenario) -- the JSON recipe POSTs the token payload to /r/scin01 then GETs /r/scview01 and semantic-verifies the token there. Same two-page shape as the second-order pair, but here the FLOW is data, not a dedicated CLI flag, and the finding carries type 'scenario'.

Phase 127 safe twin: same recipe, but the write endpoint stores the escaped value, so the viewer renders text -- the token never lands in an executable position and the scenario stays unconfirmed. The two twins use different param names (comment vs note) so each runs only its own scenario.

Phase 128: an audit pair, not an exploit pair. The page sets NO cross-origin isolation (COOP/CORP/COEP) and no framing restriction, so L7_xsleak reports the open no-cors / frame-timing / window.name surface (low/firm). The layer is opt-in, hence --audit-xs-leaks.

Phase 128 safe twin: byte-identical page plus a single hardening header (X-Frame-Options: DENY). audit_mitigations() returns None once ANY isolation family is present -- one header is all it takes to silence the audit. Note the finding is severity low, so the high/medium zero-finding gate cannot catch a regression here; the twin is verified with the flag genuinely ON.

Phase 128b: mXSS. Raw reflection + a mutating sink inside a script region (DOMParser/parseFromString) -- the layer requires BOTH, and its sink scan only looks at <script> blocks and on*= handlers. DOMParser is used instead of innerHTML on purpose: the innerHTML family is on the Trusted Types layer's list and would make the SAFE twin emit trusted_types_no_policy (medium), turning a correct case into a red gate.

Phase 128b safe twin: same page and same re-serialising script, but the value is escaped -- mutation.detect_reflection() is a verbatim substring check, so the payload never survives and the layer stays silent. The premise removed is the survival of the markup, not the sink.
